title: Restriction of scalars preserves colimits
statement:
In the situation of [def-sfb-modobj-restrict-coextend-adjunction], the functor
$\operatorname{Res}_\varphi$ preserves colimits.

proof.text: By [def-sfb-modobj-restrict-coextend-adjunction], there is an adjunction $L\dashv R$ with $L=\operatorname{Res}_\varphi\colon\Mod_{\mathcal S}(\mathcal C)\to\Mod_{\mathcal R}(\mathcal C)$ and $R=\operatorname{Coext}_\varphi$. Thus restriction is the left adjoint in this adjunction.

source.place: Part 3, coextension is right adjoint to restriction

proof.text: Let $I$ be any small category, and let $M\colon I\to\Mod_{\mathcal S}(\mathcal C)$ have a colimit $(P,(\iota_i)_i)$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-left-adjoint-preserves-colimits] to the adjunction in step 1: it says that $(\operatorname{Res}_\varphi P,(\operatorname{Res}_\varphi\iota_i)_i)$ is a colimit of $\operatorname{Res}_\varphi\circ M$ in $\Mod_{\mathcal R}(\mathcal C)$. Since $I$, $M$, and its colimit cocone were arbitrary, $\operatorname{Res}_\varphi$ preserves colimits. This asserts preservation of colimits that exist; no existence of all colimits in either module category is required.

proof_origin.place: Part 3, final implication; expanded using Stacks Tag 0038 (lemma-adjoint-exact), part (1)
